hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, a reaction is redox only if some element is oxidised and another is reduced.
Check mixture 1 first, hydrogen goes from 0 in $\text{H}_2$ to +1 in $\text{HBr}$ while bromine goes from 0 to -1.
Now track Cl in mixture 2 and Ag, I and K in mixture 3 to see if any oxidation numbers actually change or if they are just acid-base and precipitation.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for redox**

A redox reaction must show a change in oxidation number. One species is oxidised (oxidation number increases) and another is reduced (oxidation number decreases).

Rule to use:
$$\text{redox if oxidation numbers change, not redox if they stay the same}$$

**Analyse mixture 1**

Bromine + hydrogen gives hydrogen bromide. This is direct combination of two elements.

$$\text{H}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HBr}$$
Here $\text{H}$: 0 to +1 (oxidised) and $\text{Br}$: 0 to -1 (reduced). So 1 is redox.

**Analyse mixture 2**

Sodium chloride + concentrated sulfuric acid gives sodium hydrogensulfate + hydrogen chloride. This is an acid-base proton transfer.

$$\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{HCl}$$
Check states: $\text{Na}$ stays +1, $\text{Cl}$ stays -1, $\text{S}$ stays +6, $\text{O}$ stays -2. No change, so 2 is not redox.

**Analyse mixture 3 and conclude**

Potassium iodide + silver nitrate gives silver iodide precipitate + potassium nitrate. This is precipitation by ion exchange.

$$\text{KI} + \text{AgNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{AgI} + \text{KNO}_3$$
Check states: $\text{K}$ stays +1, $\text{I}$ stays -1, $\text{Ag}$ stays +1, $\text{N}$ stays +5. No change, so 3 is not redox.

Only mixture 1 is redox.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three are redox. Mixtures 2 and 3 show no change in oxidation number, they are acid-base and precipitation reactions, not electron transfer.
options.B: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 2 are redox. Mixture 2 only makes $\text{HCl}$, $\text{Cl}$ stays at -1 and $\text{S}$ stays at +6, so students who confuse any reaction of concentrated acid with redox choose this.
options.C: Incorrect. This suggests 2 and 3 are redox but excludes 1. In fact 1 is the only redox, while 2 and 3 keep all oxidation numbers constant. Precipitation of $\text{AgI}$ does not involve oxidation or reduction.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is redox because $\text{H}_2$ is oxidised to +1 and $\text{Br}_2$ is reduced to -1 in forming $\text{HBr}$. Mixtures 2 and 3 involve no change in oxidation number.
